title: Generating function of positive compositions = Xᵏ/(1−X)ᵏ
content: The header recasts the strong-composition count C(n−1, k−1) in generating-function form. A positive composition of n into k parts is g : Fin k → ℕ with every part ≥ 1 and ∑ᵢ g(i) = n. Over any commutative ring S, the ordinary generating function of these counts, P k = ∑ₙ #{g : Fin k → ℕ // (∀ i, 1 ≤ g i) ∧ ∑ i, g i = n} · Xⁿ ∈ S⟦X⟧, equals Xᵏ times the weak-composition generating function W k = 1/(1−X)ᵏ established in the parent entry — i.e. Xᵏ/(1−X)ᵏ. The Xᵏ factor is the algebraic shadow of the ±1 bijection (subtract 1 from each of the k parts), which lowers the degree by exactly k. Mathlib supplies the multiplication-by-Xᵏ coefficient rule, the parent supplies W k, and the sibling oq-03 supplies the bijection and the count; identifying the positive generating function with Xᵏ · W k is the new content.
prerequisites: Weak-composition generating function W k = 1/(1−X)ᵏ (parent entry oq-01)
The ±1 bijection positiveCompositionEquivWeak and count C(n−1, k−1) (sibling oq-03)

title: The generating function positiveCompositionGenFun and its coefficients
content: positiveCompositionGenFun S k = PowerSeries.mk (fun n => (Fintype.card {g : Fin k → ℕ // (∀ i, 1 ≤ g i) ∧ ∑ i, g i = n} : S)) packages the positive-composition counts as a formal power series over an arbitrary commutative ring S; the Fintype instance on the positive-composition subtype is imported from the sibling oq-03. The simp lemma coeff_positiveCompositionGenFun reads its n-th coefficient straight off as the cast of the count, via coeff_mk.
prerequisites: Fintype instance on the positive-composition subtype (sibling oq-03)
relatedConcepts: casting ℕ counts into a ring

title: The factored identity P k = Xᵏ · W k (every k)
content: positiveCompositionGenFun_eq proves P k = Xᵏ · W k for every k, no positivity hypothesis. By PowerSeries.ext and Mathlib's coeff_X_pow_mul', the n-th coefficient of Xᵏ · W k is coeff (n−k) (W k) when k ≤ n and 0 otherwise. In the k ≤ n branch, coeff_weakCompositionGenFun and Fintype.card_congr applied to the sibling's positiveCompositionEquivWeak k n identify #(positive comps of n) with #(weak comps of n−k). In the n < k branch, an IsEmpty proof — k positive parts force a total ≥ k > n, via Finset.sum_le_sum bounding the part-sum below by k — makes the positive count 0 (Fintype.card_eq_zero), matching the else-branch. The Xᵏ factor is literally the coeff_X_pow_mul' degree shift, the algebraic form of the ±1 bijection.
mathContext: $[X^n](X^k W_k) = \begin{cases}[X^{n-k}]W_k & k\le n\\ 0 & n<k\end{cases}$, matched coefficientwise to $\#(\text{positive comps of }n)$.
prerequisites: Finset.sum_le_sum / Fintype.card_eq_zero for the n < k emptiness branch
relatedConcepts: ±1 bijection between strong and weak compositions
degree shift as multiplication by Xᵏ

title: Xᵏ/(1−X)ᵏ and the residue relation P k · (1−X)ᵏ = Xᵏ
content: positiveCompositionGenFun_eq_X_pow_mul_invOneSubPow rewrites W k by the parent's weakCompositionGenFun_eq_invOneSubPow (0 < k) to present P k as Xᵏ · invOneSubPow S k = Xᵏ/(1−X)ᵏ. positiveCompositionGenFun_mul_one_sub_pow multiplies P k by (1−X)ᵏ, reassociates, and applies the parent's weakCompositionGenFun_mul_one_sub_pow (W k · (1−X)ᵏ = 1) to conclude P k · (1−X)ᵏ = Xᵏ — the formal statement that P k is Xᵏ times the inverse of (1−X)ᵏ. The 0 < k hypothesis is inherited from the parent's weak-series inverse relation, not from the factored identity.
prerequisites: Mathlib's invOneSubPow S k as the inverse unit of (1−X)ᵏ

title: Reading off the coefficients: C(n−1, k−1)
content: coeff_positiveCompositionGenFun_eq_card restates the coefficient as the positive-composition count, and coeff_positiveCompositionGenFun_eq_choose specializes it to the closed form C(n−1, k−1) for 0 < k ≤ n by rewriting through the sibling's card_positiveComposition. These are the term-by-term face of the generating-function identity — the classical statement that the compositions-into-k-positive-parts numbers are the coefficients of Xᵏ/(1−X)ᵏ. The closed form is stated only for k ≤ n, where ℕ truncation does not distort C(n−1, k−1); for n < k the count is 0 (handled by the factored identity).
prerequisites: card_positiveComposition (sibling oq-03): C(n−1, k−1) for 0 < k ≤ n
